newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: J.Martins expands in Poland - paper.
newsitem.headline: J.Martins expands in Poland - paper.

text.p: Portugal's second biggest retailer Jeronimo Martins is expanding its activities in Poland and has decided not to pursue investments in Hungary, a senior management source was quoted as saying.

The company plans to raise the number of its discount stores in Poland to 220 and cash-and-carry stores to 68 by the end of 1997, up from 140 discount and 57 cash-and-carry stores now, the source told Wednesday's Diario de Noticias newspaper.
He said Jeronimo Martins's total investment in Poland this year could be up to six billion escudos ($35 million).
Asked what progress had been made in talks to buy a chain of cash-and-carry stores in Hungary, the source said: "Hungary has a macroeconomic situation far less favourable than Poland."
Jeronimo Martins believed that economic growth would be slower in Hungary than in Poland and that there was already a well-established network of competitors in Hungary.
Jeronimo Martins's president Alexandre Soares dos Santos told Diario de Noticias in an interview last December that the company was negotiating to buy a chain a six cash-and-carry stores in Hungary.
Company spokesmen were not immediately available to confirm today's newspaper report.
